On 2023-05-22, the user asked about human sensory perception and cognition. The assistant described five main senses: vision (light and color; visual information supports learning, memory, and pattern recognition), hearing (sound; supports language, communication, and learning), taste (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami; helps identify food and avoid harmful substances), smell (odors; helps identify substances and can evoke memories and emotions), and touch or somatosensation (including pressure, temperature, and pain; helps people understand and navigate the physical world). The assistant noted that sensory information combines to shape perception, thinking, behavior, emotion, and motivation.

On 2023-05-22, the user asked how senses influence emotion and behavior. The assistant explained that sensory stimuli can trigger emotions—for example, seeing a loved one may evoke happiness and love, while an unpleasant smell may evoke disgust. Sensory input can also prompt protective behavior, such as pulling away from something hot or covering the ears or moving away after a loud noise. Positive or negative associations and memories can shape preferences and choices about scents, flavors, and textures.
records.topic: sensory influences on emotion and behavior

records.text: On 2023-05-22, the user asked whether external factors such as drugs or injury can affect sensory perception. The assistant said drugs, injuries, and diseases can alter or impair perception: alcohol can affect balance and coordination; LSD can cause vivid visual hallucinations; head or brain injuries can impair vision, hearing, or multiple senses; diabetes can damage nerves in the feet and reduce sensation; and Alzheimer's disease can affect perception, memory, and recognition. The assistant noted that some resulting conditions can be treated or managed, while sensory problems may affect quality of life and daily functioning.

On 2023-05-22, the user asked what could be inferred from a TiDB execution plan. The plan projected bookmark and several component fields from table `bbbb`, with a root `Limit` and an `IndexRangeScan` on index `f_bookmark(f_bookmark)`. It also showed a TiKV selection applying equality on `f_bookmark` and a `TableRowIDScan`. The root projection reported 1,000,000 actual rows, 6.09 seconds, and one loop; the index scan reported about 5,191,584 processed keys, while the coprocessor limit and selection showed millions of rows processed. The assistant described the plan as a SELECT execution tree and explained the roles of projection, limit, index scan, execution information, memory, and disk columns.

On 2023-05-23, the user provided a proposal section titled “Browser Requirements,” referencing “Tabla 4. Requisitos mínimos de la Aplicación, Sistema Operativo.” The text argued that the browser list included extremely outdated versions, some over 15 years old (citing Opera 9, released June 2006, before the iPhone’s introduction); that old browsers lack protection from current vulnerabilities and modern web security protocols such as TLS 1.2; and that modern web technology is needed for a clear, fast, reliable, dynamic experience, especially for bidders. The user said their company generally guarantees reliable functionality only on the latest common browser versions, with possible support for recent previous versions. The proposed Spanish-language recommendation was to replace the enumerated versions with: “Admitir versiones actuales de Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, Google Chrome y Safari,” noting browser release cycles are short.

On 2023-05-23, the user provided a proposal section titled “General Software Requirements.” It argued that software requirements sometimes prescribe overly specific feature implementations, limiting provider innovation and ability to meet the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones (IFT)’s needs. As an example, the user quoted a page 9 requirement that a bidder receiving a text message or digital file in their work inbox must see a pop-up and check an acceptance checkbox before reading, downloading, and unlocking the application, even if the item remains archived in the inbox. The user explained that alternative workflows can achieve notification and ensure messages are read; forcing a provider to change a thoroughly tested workflow can raise implementation costs and introduce software defects. The user recommended allowing tenderers to propose alternative implementations that meet the same goals in their RFP responses. They further argued that implementation-specific requirements may favor a vendor that already built a feature in the prescribed way, whereas flexibility supports fairer, more competitive vendor selection and helps protect IFT from perceptions of favoritism. The assistant rendered the section in Spanish.

On May 23, 2023, the user drafted a Spanish proposal section titled “3. Planificación del Desarrollo del Software,” referencing “3.3 Fechas de eventos relevantes y entrega de la prestación de los Servicios, Módulo II.” The draft says the time required for this project phase depends on the auction design selected. The proposed 20 working days to develop use cases and a traceability matrix, and 20 working days to deliver the application in a QA environment, are feasible for most standard spectrum auction formats; a bespoke design or very complex auction process may require more time.

The user proposed allowing flexibility in the software development schedule and explicitly permitting a later extension, for example at the milestone “Selección de mecanismo de asignación por parte del Instituto.” The user also proposed discussing the timeline implications of auction-design recommendations in the report delivered in Módulo I.
